practice_span: Since I was fifteen. It has been twenty-five years now.
primary_material: Vegetable-tanned leather, babul bark, lime, leather braid and thick thread.
material_origin: Leather from a nearby tannery, babul bark from the surrounding villages.
material_in_hands: Good leather springs back when bent and has a faint smell of babul. The sole sits tight under the hammer.
material_feels_wrong: Chrome leather feels slick to the hand and smells of chemicals. Fold it and a white line appears.
correction_action: I send such leather back. Leather that gets wet in the rain I dry only in the shade, not in the sun.
pride_moment: A wrestler from Kolhapur used my chappal for seven years and brought it for repair. He said, “The foot has made its home in it.”
loss_if_stopped: Generations of hand measure and braid work would be gone. Only the printed name ‘Kolhapuri’ would remain.
concern_anchor: Big companies use our design. No name for us, no name for the village, and certainly no payment.
outsider_misunderstanding: People think this is a cheap village chappal. One pair takes time, measure and a judgment of the leather.
learning_story: Once in a hurry I stitched wet leather. Within a week the customer's chappal shrank. I gave the money back. Since then I don't take the needle to leather until it has dried.
